title: Monitoring storage
subtitle: Space, open files, and disk I/O — flip to reveal meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: Free space per mounted filesystem (Size / Used / Avail / Use% / Mounted on)
cards.notes: Answers “is / full?” One row per mount. Does not say which directory ate the space — that is du.

cards.meaning: Percentage of the filesystem that is used — what paging/alerts usually watch
cards.notes: Alert on Use%, not only Avail. Each Mounted on path can fill independently.

cards.meaning: Disk usage: one human-readable total per argument (-s summarize, -h human)
cards.notes: Typical hunt: du -sh /* then drill into /var/* until you find the fat directory.

cards.meaning: df = which mount is full; du = which folder inside it
cards.notes: Memory hook: disks vs folders. Deleted-but-still-open files can make df and du disagree until the process closes them.

cards.meaning: List open files belonging to active processes (everything is a file on Linux)
cards.notes: No options = all open files, all processes (huge). Need root to see other users’ files.

cards.meaning: Processes that have this file/path open
cards.notes: Useful when a path will not unmount or a binary is still held open.

cards.meaning: Open files for processes whose command name starts with name
cards.notes: -c filters by command name. Pair with -i for network-focused views.

cards.meaning: List Internet network files — TCP/UDP connections and listeners
cards.notes: Who is listening or connected. Network sockets as open files.

cards.meaning: A file deleted from the directory tree but still open by a process keeps the blocks until close
cards.example: df shows full; du does not find the dir; use lsof (e.g. +L1 later)
cards.notes: du shrinks only after the process closes the handle. Classic “where did space go?” trap.

cards.meaning: Per-disk read/write statistics (totals, merged ops, sectors, time, current IO)
cards.notes: Report for each block device (sda, dm-0, …). How hard disks have been working.

cards.meaning: Detailed read/write statistics for one partition
cards.notes: Narrower than -d: one partition name. Memory hook: -d = each disk; -p name = one partition.

cards.meaning: I/O load with timestamp — CPU averages plus Device table (tps, kB/s)
cards.notes: From sysstat (like sar/mpstat). Watch iowait together with tps and df Use%.

cards.meaning: Device I/O only — no CPU block (tps, kB read/write rates and totals)
cards.notes: Disks-only view. Live sample: iostat -d 1 5 (every 1s, 5 times).

cards.meaning: Transfers (I/O requests) per second for a device
cards.notes: Request rate, not only throughput. Pair with kB_read/s and kB_wrtn/s.

cards.meaning: Read and write throughput for the device
cards.notes: kB_read / kB_wrtn without /s are totals since boot when no interval is given. dm-0 is often LVM on sda.
